body:
`tests/unit/test_1094_failed_conversion_imports_original.py::TestConversionDeadline::test_convert_book_passes_the_deadline_to_the_converter`
failed once in a full local `python3 -m pytest tests/unit/ -q` (1 failed, 5924 passed), and passes
everywhere else it was tried.

Not reproduced:
- the file alone: 49 passed
- paired with `test_1009_...` and with `test_1074_...`: 66 and 53 passed
- the single test by node id: 1 passed
- CI "Fast Tests (Smoke + Unit)" on the same commit (6e23c316a): SUCCESS

So it is order- or ambient-state-dependent, not a defect in the deadline arithmetic itself, and it
does not currently gate anything. Deliberately NOT bisected -- the coarse bisect was abandoned
rather than guessed at, so the polluter is unknown. Recording it because an intermittent local red
that CI never sees is exactly the shape that later gets dismissed as "just flaky" and then wedges a
tick.

Worth noting for whoever picks this up: an explicit multi-file invocation
(`pytest f1.py f2.py ... f7.py`) reported `collected 0 items` with no error, while the same files
individually collect fine. That is either a second small bug in the harness or a shell artifact in
how the list was built; it made the obvious bisect route unreliable and should be checked first.
title: test_convert_book_passes_the_deadline_to_the_converter fails only in a full serial local run
